html:
Jamestown was the first lasting English settlement in the Americas, founded in May 1607 on the James River in Virginia by the Virginia Company of London. It was the capital of the Colony of Virginia until 1699.

About a hundred men and boys built a fort on a marshy island in the land of the Powhatan paramount chiefdom. Bad water, disease and hunger killed most of them. John Smith forced the survivors to work and bargained for corn with the Powhatan and neighbours such as the Chickahominy. In the "Starving Time" of the winter of 1609 to 1610 most of the settlers died.

Tobacco saved the colony. John Rolfe planted a sweet West Indian strain from about 1612, and the tobacco boom followed. Rolfe married Pocahontas, Powhatan's daughter, in 1614. In 1619 the first elected assembly in English America met in Jamestown's church, and the same year the first enslaved Africans reached Virginia.

The town was burned during Bacon's Rebellion in 1676. After the statehouse burned again in 1698, the capital moved to Williamsburg, and Jamestown slowly emptied. Together with Plymouth, founded in 1620, it is remembered as the start of British North America.
sum: Jamestown was the first lasting English settlement in the Americas, founded in May 1607 on the James River in Virginia by the Virginia Company of London. It was the capital of the Colony of Virginia until 1699.
